newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee marks time in search of direction.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee marks time in search of direction.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee which was quoted at 57.11 to the dollar at 0400 GMT, remained untraded nearly two hours after the market opened as dealers searched for direction.
The rupee closed at the same level on Friday.
"Even those who has genuine import covering wait to see which way the rate will move before coming in," said a Sampath Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by 3.25 local cents in response to foreign gains. Buying and selling prices were fixed at 56.0291 and 57.1610
Caution is prompted by the exchange rate being so close to the Central Bank top level, the Sampath Bank dealer said.
Dealers said import covering should maintain the exchange rate at current levels.
"Traditionally, there is enough genuine demand to keep the dollar high in the last quarter of the year," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Overnight call money was at 15 percent after opening at 16, due to a big lender entering the market, dealers said.
